identity_scope: SHA-256 on exact publisher HTTP response bodies and on whitespace-normalized visible UTF-8 excerpts. HTML navigation may change on a versioned scientific abstract. An unchanged body alone cannot establish the scientific claim. Undated publisher pages have null publication dates. Open pages establish reading access only.

sources.title: Beyond Leaderboard Ranks: Selecting Software Engineering Agents Under Budget Constraints
sources.publisher: Srinath Srinivasan and Tim Menzies via arXiv
sources.excerpt: Under advance knowledge of task costs, successive halving reaches our uncertainty-aware selection target on SWE-bench using 6.6% of exhaustive evaluation spend
sources.scope: The abstract reports 58,197 raw run–task records and a paired analysis of seven retained benchmarks. Across the seven the authors report unresolved differences at 27 of 35 neighboring frontier steps. Their 6.6% replay required advance task costs and their uncertainty-aware target. See hal-methods for the retained populations.
sources.limitation: An exact-best objective or unknown task costs reduces the reported benefit. This simulation supplies no price for archived public outcome files, current provider use or accepted MONTREAL.AI patches.
sources.earlier_condition: Leaderboards, conventional sampling, complete evaluation and successive halving predate this study.
sources.independent_test: Compare grouped SQL on complete released data. Require fresh portfolio outcomes and measured execution costs before evaluating adaptive sampling on actual internal work.

sources.title: Beyond Leaderboard Ranks, data and study design
sources.publisher: Srinath Srinivasan and Tim Menzies via arXiv
sources.excerpt: 34 runs evaluated on 48 of its original 50 tasks
sources.scope: Reconstruction recovered 58,197 records on 11 benchmarks. Filtering coverage and cost yielded 20,633 retained cells on seven. SWE-bench Verified Mini supplied 34 runs on 48 common tasks.
sources.limitation: A Mini subset with reconstructed costs cannot price or qualify two different submissions on the complete 500-instance Verified corpus. Statistical non-rejection does not establish equal performance.
sources.earlier_condition: Trace reconstruction and per-run cost re-estimation distinguish this study from simply reading a published leaderboard.
sources.independent_test: Use the full 500-task roster for the separate internal question. For a future cost-constrained agent trial compare simple successive halving under both prospective and oracle cost information.

sources.title: SWE-bench Verified
sources.excerpt: A human-validated subset of 500 SWE-bench instances
sources.scope: The 500-instance set was screened by humans. The complete leaderboard mixes systems. A bash-only leaderboard fixes the basic agent loop and documents relevant scaffold-version differences.
sources.limitation: A common harness alone does not equalize model settings, economic inputs, task exposure or population transfer.
sources.earlier_condition: Human-curated issue tests, repository metadata and standard database aggregation already existed.
sources.independent_test: Bind both submission labels and all 500 issue IDs to the official roster. Weight repositories explicitly and preserve A-only and B-only counts.

sources.title: Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding capabilities
sources.locator: Background, findings on a targeted audit and training exposure
sources.excerpt: at least 59.4% of the audited problems have flawed test cases that reject functionally correct submissions
sources.scope: OpenAI examined a 27.6% subset selected for frequent model failures and found test defects in at least 59.4% of those audited problems. It also observed output consistent with prior exposure in the frontier models tested.
sources.limitation: The reported defect fraction applies to the selected hard subset. It cannot be imputed to all 500 tasks, an individual submission or a new internal task.
sources.earlier_condition: OpenAI and the maintainers released the human-filtered benchmark in August 2024.
sources.independent_test: Use archived passes solely for the registered historical estimand. Freeze freshly authored, independently reviewed beneficiary tests for any deployment adoption claim.

sources.title: Public Alerts User Guide, version 30 change log
sources.excerpt: they are now distributed exclusively over Kafka as JSON from GCN and as Avro from SCiMMA
sources.scope: For current delivery the guide describes withdrawal of VOEvent/GCN Classic in favour of Kafka with distinct GCN and SCiMMA representations.
sources.limitation: The release date and historical index do not establish delivery to any named observer. Forecast observing-run dates in historical release notes are proposals.
sources.earlier_condition: Official notices and retractions existed before the change in distribution. The public archive and current feed have different interfaces.
sources.independent_test: Use immutable archival records for history. Qualify a current-format decoder, authorized access and actual ingestion times separately for field use.

sources.title: GCN missions: LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA
sources.version: Current NASA mission documentation, retrieved 18 November 2026
sources.locator: JSON-Serialized GCN Notices Types, RETRACTION row
sources.excerpt: After human analysis/evaluation, a retraction will be issued if trigger is not astrophysical.
sources.scope: NASA documents official LVK alert types, including withdrawal by the collaboration, and links to the collaboration’s schema. The typed field supports a conventional archive-and-SQL comparator.
sources.limitation: A withdrawal is the collaboration’s classification of a candidate. A second broker or circular may transmit the same judgment.
sources.earlier_condition: Existing specialist software and human operators can already use typed official retractions.
sources.independent_test: Replay prior and later issue cutoffs with an event-bound authority. Compare shadow queue decisions with direct SQL on the same notices.

sources.title: From observations to forecasts: bringing AI-DOP into real time
sources.excerpt: 30-hours of observations in six-hour windows to establish an initial state
sources.scope: The ECMWF team reports a prototype connected to its real-time processing infrastructure. Forecasts start from thirty hours of recent observations using daily experimental runs at two spatial resolutions.
sources.limitation: The prototype team has infrastructure not established for the beneficiary. Local skill, access to past issue-time grids, publication timestamps, data rights and operational availability require examination.
sources.earlier_condition: Numerical IFS and operational AIFS already deliver weather forecasts. Past-case direct observation prediction experiments preceded the real-time prototype.
sources.independent_test: An authorized trial needs independently timestamped grids and withheld outcome observations. Compare the best existing product that had actually arrived by each deadline.

sources.title: AIFS Machine Learning data
sources.version: AIFS Single and ensemble v2, documented upgrade 12 May 2026
sources.excerpt: operationally since 25 February 2025 and was upgraded from AIFS Single v1.1 to AIFS Single v2 on 12 May 2026
sources.scope: ECMWF identifies operational deterministic and ensemble baselines, data formats, published real-time access and separate registration arrangements for historical MARS data.
sources.limitation: Its AIFS terms and access do not transfer automatically to the experimental AI-DOP prototype. Actual arrival time at the receiving desk remains unknown.
sources.earlier_condition: The deterministic AIFS product has run operationally since February 2025 and the ensemble since July 2025.
sources.independent_test: Use versioned IFS and AIFS as complete forecast alternatives and account for acquisition, storage and operator time at the same issue cutoff.

sources.title: ForgeKernel: Self-Evolving Kernels Catching and Surpassing Experts and Agents
sources.publisher: Yaojian Chen and coauthors via arXiv
sources.scope: The authors report that their system beat the per-operation public best on the public cases of eight level-4 CANN operators on Ascend 910C. They also report separate NVIDIA configuration results.
sources.limitation: The percentage refers to the Ascend public suite geometric mean. It is not a minimum per-operation gain, an application result or independently measured hardware performance here.
sources.earlier_condition: Vendor kernels, specialist tuning, compilers and prior kernel-generating systems were already practical alternatives.
sources.independent_test: Profile an actual authorized hardware deployment. On representative held-out shapes, measure end-to-end correctness, total device occupancy and maintenance against the best vendor implementation.

sources.title: Inference-Sufficient Representations for High-Throughput Measurement: Lessons from Lossless Compression Benchmarks in 4D-STEM
sources.publisher: Ondrej Dyck and coauthors via arXiv
sources.locator: Abstract, measured codecs and inference-driven representations
sources.excerpt: 13 lossless compression implementations across 5 representative datasets
sources.scope: The authors tested five 4D-STEM datasets with ten runs per method. Their Blosc/Zstd comparison showed compression ratios comparable to gzip-9 and faster encoding and reads. The authors propose representations tailored to scientific inference.
sources.limitation: Measured benefits apply to the tested lossless codecs and datasets. The suggested change of representation lacks demonstrated preservation of a new beneficiary’s future inferences.
sources.earlier_condition: HDF5, gzip, Blosc and Zstd precede the preprint. Replacing a slow codec may already remove the storage bottleneck.
sources.independent_test: Try a reversible conventional codec on the receiving instrument’s access pattern. Keep the original and verify every scientifically required calculation before any information removal.
